sentences.en: Before we start today, this episode is about race and free speech.
sentences.zh: 在我们今天开始之前，本期节目将探讨种族与言论自由。

sentences.en: It includes sounds from the violence in Charlottesville, as well as a racial epithet.
sentences.zh: 其中包含夏洛茨维尔暴力事件的现场录音，以及针对特定种族的侮辱性词汇。

sentences.en: If you have small kids with you, please save this one for later.
sentences.zh: 如果您身边有幼童，请稍后再收听这一集。

sentences.en: A few weeks ago, the words Charlottesville
sentences.zh: 几周前，“夏洛茨维尔”这个词

sentences.en: and tiki torches weren't national symbols you'd associate with white supremacy.
sentences.zh: 和“火把”还不是你会将之与白人至上主义联系在一起的国家符号。

sentences.en: Today, those words convey a very specific scene.
sentences.zh: 而如今，这些词唤起的是一幅非常具体的画面。

sentences.en: We begin with the deadly chaos on the streets of Charlottesville, Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我们从弗吉尼亚州夏洛茨维尔街头发生的致命混乱开始说起。

sentences.en: Yesterday's dueling rallies turned deadly when a car plowed into a group of those who opposed the alt-right.
sentences.zh: 由于一辆汽车冲入反另类右翼人群，昨天针锋相对的集会演变成了致命事件。

sentences.en: It was a weekend of street battles and stark displays of racism.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充斥着街头冲突和赤裸裸种族主义的周末。

sentences.en: Photos of enraged white men using the Nazi salute and marching with torches shocked many Americans.
sentences.zh: 愤怒的白人男子行纳粹礼并举着火把游行的照片震惊了许多美国人。

sentences.en: And since then, many of us have been doing a lot of soul-searching.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，我们中的许多人一直在进行深刻的反思。

sentences.en: And as a nation, what do we tolerate?
sentences.zh: 作为这个国家，我们容忍的底线是什么？

sentences.en: Today, we want to zoom in on a specific issue that grows out of the events in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们想要聚焦于一个从夏洛茨维尔事件中衍生出的具体问题。

sentences.en: The Constitution upholds the rights of Americans to say almost anything, no matter how distasteful,
sentences.zh: 宪法维护美国人发表几乎任何言论的权利，无论这些言论多么令人反感，

sentences.en: without censure from legislatures, the police, or the courts.
sentences.zh: 而免受立法机关、警方或法院的审查。

sentences.en: Our protections for speech, even hate-filled, vitriolic speech, go further than most nations.
sentences.zh: 我们对言论的保护——甚至是充满仇恨、尖酸刻薄的言论——比大多数国家都要走得更远。

sentences.en: In recent weeks, many people have made free speech arguments to defend the white supremacists who descended on Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 最近几周，许多人以言论自由为由，为涌入夏洛茨维尔的白人至上主义者辩护。

sentences.en: Is hate speech protected under the Constitution, in a word?
sentences.zh: 简而言之，仇恨言论受宪法保护吗？

sentences.en: Free speech may give them the right to do this, but...
sentences.zh: 言论自由或许赋予了他们这样做的权利，但是……

sentences.en: Are they not familiar with the First Amendment?
sentences.zh: 难道他们对第一修正案一无所知吗？

sentences.en: There's a fine line between free speech and hate speech.
sentences.zh: 言论自由与仇恨言论之间有一条细微的界线。

sentences.en: But hold on, we can't have that conversation, or any conversation, until we both agree that we have the right to say what we believe.
sentences.zh: 但等等，在我们双方都同意我们有权表达自己的信念之前，我们无法进行这场对话，也无法进行任何对话。

sentences.en: And that we're not going to be punished for doing that.
sentences.zh: 并且我们不会因为这样做而受到惩罚。

sentences.en: Are these arguments motivated by principle, or something less heroic?
sentences.zh: 这些争论是出于原则，还是出于某些不那么崇高的动机？

sentences.en: New psychological research suggests that people's motivations might not be what they seem.
sentences.zh: 新的心理学研究表明，人们的动机可能并不像他们表现出来的那么简单。

sentences.en: And that's true no matter where you fall on the political spectrum.
sentences.zh: 无论你在政治光谱上处于什么位置，这都是事实。

sentences.en: People pull out free speech as a defense when they're defending racist speech,
sentences.zh: 当人们在为种族主义言论辩护时，他们会搬出言论自由作为借口，

sentences.en: but not when they're defending simply aggressive or negative speech.
sentences.zh: 但当他们为单纯的好斗或消极言论辩护时却不会这样。

sentences.en: Today on Hidden Brain, what we're really saying when we say we defend free speech,
sentences.zh: 今天在“隐藏大脑”中，我们将探讨当我们声称捍卫言论自由时，我们真正想表达的是什么，

sentences.en: and how the words we use and the things we say shape the culture in which we live.
sentences.zh: 以及我们使用的词汇和所说的话如何塑造了我们生活的文化。

sentences.en: Chris Crandall is a professor of psychology at the University of Kansas.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·克兰达尔是堪萨斯大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: He studies prejudice and has looked at how we use free speech claiMs.
sentences.zh: 他专门研究偏见，并探讨了我们如何利用言论自由的主张。
